label: D1 after the previous trial reached S2
explanation: Fires only at D1 (GO/D2 effectively never) and only when the previous trial landed in state S2; it is essentially never active at D1 after S1 (0 activations after unrewarded S1, ~0 after rewarded S1). Nearly all missed activations (17% of mass) are D1 steps of the window first trial (rel -3), where prev_state is not recorded in the window (-1); (phase == D1) & (prev_state != 1) scores the same dev F1 (0.817) with recall/mass recall ~1.0, so the feature is really a clean D1-after-S2 detector. Magnitude: strongest after unrewarded S2 visits (prec 0.93, largest activations, e.g. after common-unrewarded a2 trials); weaker after rewarded S2; the false positives are mainly D1 steps inside long confident streaks of rewarded common a2->S2 trials, where activation drops to zero or near it, and it rises later in episodes (ep_trial 50+). Uses only observed variables (previous reached state and reward).

issues: All factual claims hold on dev. GO has 19 activations out of 160,646 and D2 has 0. D1 after S1 has precision 0 in both the rewarded and unrewarded cases. Unrewarded S2 has precision 0.928, recall 0.342 and mass recall 0.472, against 0.768 / 0.465 / 0.358 for rewarded S2, so activations are larger after unrewarded S2 visits. The rel -3 D1 steps hold 0.170 of the activation mass, and the variant prev_state != 1 gets mass recall 1.000.
The reported test scores reproduce for (phase==D1)&(prev_state==2): P 0.837, R 0.805, F1 0.821, mass recall 0.829. The prev_state != 1 variant gets test F1 0.823 and mass recall 1.000.

There is one systematic false-positive class, and the explanation only partly describes it. It is a timing effect within the episode: precision of D1 & prev_state==2 is 0.64 in ep_trials 10-49 but 0.97 in ep_trials 50+ (test: 0.69 below trial 50 vs 0.97 at 50+). It is worst for rewarded S2 visits before trial 50 (precision 0.56). The explanation gives the cause as 'long confident rewarded common a2->S2 runs' and separately says the feature is 'more frequent later'. The episode-time split is the stronger factor. Removing the confident-run class changes little: test F1 goes from 0.823 to 0.829. So the gap is real, but it is a gating effect on the same detector rather than a different trigger.

The prev_reward==1 & prev_common==0 subset (rare rewarded S2) has precision 0.9997. The feature is reliable when S2 was reached by an a1 rare transition, so it tracks the reached state, not the action: prev_action==2 alone scores F1 0.56.
The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate, and no future variables are involved.
